newsitem.title: UK: SCARDINO SUBMITS 18.2 MILLION STG BID FOR FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SCARDINO SUBMITS 18.2 MILLION STG BID FOR FOREST.

text.p: English Premier League soccer club Nottingham Forest received another bid for 18.2 million pounds for 90 percent ownership from a consortium represented by London-based American journalist Albert Scardino.

"It is the last of the great sleeping giants of English football in terms of business operations...the opportunities in terms of media and sport development are very exciting," Scardino said on Sunday.
"If you can bring together the City's financial power with Forest's passion for the team and for the game, you could create a potent mix."
He said he did not expect to manage Forest but to encourage the institutions to get involved. "My role will be advisory."
The offer values Forest at 20.3 million stg and Scardino said it would float as soon as it was "practically possible".
"We submitted a formal commitment to the board on Friday and distributed the detailed proposal to the shareholders," Scardino, who is husband of Pearson chief executive Marjorie, said.
The 203 Forest shareholders have solicited bids for investment in the club or purchase of the club, Scardino said. He said six shares were held by the company secretary.
Mercury Asset Management and Electra Fleming Ltd are part of Scardino's consortium which rivals a bid from Nigel Wray, chairman of property group Burford and owner of Saracens rugby union club.
Wray's consortium, Bridgford, also includes former Tottenham Hotspur chairman Irving Scholar, football author Phil Soar and developer Julian Markham.

The Daily Telegraph on Saturday said Bridgford was offering shareholders two options. One involved investing 15 million stg providing 7.0 million stg of bank loans and offering shareholders 10 percent of the equity or a total of 1.7 million stg if they elect to sell.
The alternative would invest 13 million stg and provide 7.0 million stg of bank loans and 20 percent for shareholders who would share 3.25 million stg from selling.
Both options involve a stock market flotation within six months.
The two legally binding offers will be considered at a general meeting on February 24 in Nottingham and will require a 75 percent majority to win the bid.
Video and film executive Grant Bovey was thought to have put in a bid for about 20 million stg but Scardino said Bovey never submitted a binding offer.
Meanwhile The Daily Telegraph said Railways millionaire Sandy Anderson whose 13 million stg bid was backed by the Forest board but defeated by shareholders pulled out on Saturday.

Manchester United set the proverbial ball rolling with a flotation in 1991 and now other football clubs have followed suit. Leeds United , Sunderland and Southampton have floated while Newcastle is still in the planning stages.
